subject: Linguistics
title: Prototype Theory
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Prototype Theory.

hook.text: Is a penguin a bird? Technically yes—but it doesn't match your mental image of 'bird.'

buildup.text: Prototype theory says categories have best examples (prototypes) and fuzzier members.

discovery.text: Rosch showed that people rate robins as better birds than penguins—categories have internal structure.

twist.text: This challenges the classical view where membership is all-or-nothing based on features.

climax.text: Prototype effects appear everywhere: 'murder' is a more prototypical crime than 'jaywalking.'

punchline.text: Categories have centers and edges—not sharp lines.

quiz.question: What does prototype theory say about categories?
options: They have better and worse examples
